mainTopic: The southwest corner of the מזבח for the bird חטאת and the מנחה, and which bird-offering services may be done anywhere on the מזבח
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה: a כהן normally circles the מזבח and comes down on the left, but for three services at the southwest corner he goes straight there and turns back on his heels. The גמרא asks how we know the bird חטאת is done at the southwest corner. רבי יהושע answers from a פסוק that calls a מנחה a חטאת, so each borrows a rule from the other: the מנחה needs the north, and the חטאת goes at the southwest corner. To show where the מנחה itself goes, the גמרא brings a ברייתא on the words לפני ה׳ and אל פני המזבח. The first view brings it to the tip of the southwest corner. רבי אליעזר instead chooses the south side, using the rule that we follow the reading that fulfills both phrases. רב אשי explains that this works because this תנא holds the whole מזבח stood in the north. Next, רב אשי explains the משנה's 'valid in any place': the pinching may be anywhere, but the sprinkling belongs at the southwest corner. A matching ברייתא is quoted. The גמרא starts rereading it so that 'anywhere' refers to squeezing out the blood, and that rereading continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How the כהנים walk on the מזבח, and the three exceptions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes: normally a כהן circles the מזבח and comes down on the left side, but for three services he goes straight up to the southwest corner and turns back on his heels.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they circle around and come down on the left side, except for someone going up for these three services, who would go up and come down by turning on his heel.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the משנה. It describes the normal walking route on the מזבח and three exceptions where the כהן goes straight to the southwest corner and comes right back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a כהן goes up the ramp, turns right, walks all the way around the מזבח, and comes down on the left. For the three services done at the southwest corner, that corner is right by the ramp. So he walks straight there, turns around in place, and retraces his steps.

keyTerms.meaning: they circle around (the מזבח)
by way of the left side
on the heel: turning around in place and going back the same way

phrases.english: And they circle around and go down by way of the left;
except for one who goes up for these three —
phrases.notes: "These three" are the services the משנה just listed, all done at the southwest corner.

phrases.english: who would go up and come down on the heel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continuation of the משנה that began on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The normal route on the מזבח is to circle and descend on the left. For the three southwest-corner services, the כהן goes straight there and returns on his heels.

steps.title: Where do we learn the southwest corner rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking for the source of the משנה's rule that the bird חטאת is done at the southwest corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about the source in the תורה for doing the bird חטאת at the southwest corner. This sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated a location rule without giving a source. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches that the חטאת belongs at the southwest corner.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: גמרא: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the משנה's rule that the bird חטאת is done at the southwest corner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of a rule in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for doing the חטאת at the southwest corner of the מזבח.

steps.title: A פסוק calls the מנחה a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע quotes a פסוק about the poor person's flour offering that calls it a חטאת. This shows that חטאת and מנחה are linked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: The פסוק says, "He shall not put oil on it, and he shall not put frankincense on it, for it is a חטאת." So a חטאת is called a מנחה, and a מנחה is called a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers with a פסוק about a flour offering brought by a very poor person. The פסוק calls this flour offering a חטאת, which links the two kinds of offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The poor person's offering is flour, so it is really a מנחה, yet the תורה calls it a חטאת. רבי יהושע reads this as a two-way link between מנחה and חטאת. That link lets us carry rules from one to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: sin offering
flour (meal) offering
frankincense
is called

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a מנחה actually becomes a חטאת. The point is only that the תורה uses one name for the other, so their rules can be compared.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said: The verse states:
"He shall not put oil upon it,"
"and he shall not put frankincense upon it,"
"for it is a sin offering" —
a sin offering is called a meal offering,
and a meal offering is called a sin offering;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 by bringing a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 5:11 calls a מנחה a חטאת, so the two are linked and can share rules.

steps.title: Comparing חטאת and מנחה in both directions
steps.stepSummary: Using the link, each offering borrows a rule from the other: the מנחה needs the north like a חטאת, and the חטאת goes at the southwest corner like a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as a חטאת needs the north, so too a מנחה needs the north. And just as a מנחה is at the southwest corner, so too a חטאת is at the southwest corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what the link teaches, applying it both ways. This gives the answer to our question: the חטאת is done at the southwest corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חטאת already has a known rule that it needs the north, so the מנחה gets that rule too. The מנחה already has a known place, the southwest corner, so the חטאת gets that place too. The second half is the answer to the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: requires
the north side of the עזרה
the southwest corner of the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The חטאת is done at the southwest corner because the תורה links it to the מנחה, which is brought near the מזבח at that corner.

phrases.english: Just as a sin offering requires the north —
so too a meal offering requires the north,
and just as a meal offering is at the southwest corner —
so too a sin offering is at the southwest corner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical comparisons from the link established in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חטאת is done at the southwest corner, learned from the מנחה.

steps.title: How do we know the מנחה goes at the southwest corner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn the rule for the מנחה itself, since the חטאת rule was learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the מנחה itself, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. The חטאת's place was learned from the מנחה, so now we need a source for the מנחה's own place at the southwest corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 4 only works if the מנחה's location is already known. The גמרא checks that foundation by asking for its source.

keyTerms.meaning: itself
from where do we learn it?

phrases.english: And the meal offering itself, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the assumption used in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the מנחה is brought near the מזבח at the southwest corner.

steps.title: A ברייתא: not the west, but "in front of the מזבח"
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק about the מנחה. "Before ה׳" could suggest the west side, but "in front of the מזבח" corrects this and points to the south side.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "Before ה׳" — you might think this means on the west side. So the פסוק says, "in front of the מזבח."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to find the מנחה's place. The ברייתא first considers the west side, then uses the words "in front of the מזבח" to reject that idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Before ה׳" sounds like the side facing the היכל, which is the west. But the פסוק also says "in front of the מזבח," meaning the side where you face the מזבח as you approach, which is the south side by the ramp. Together these words point toward the southwest corner.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have thought
the פסוק teaches (to correct that idea)
in front of the מזבח

phrases.english: As it is taught: "Before the Lord" —
one might think it is at the west?
The verse states: "In front of the altar."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by bringing a ברייתא on ויקרא 6:7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא rejects the west side using the words "in front of the מזבח," which point to the south side by the ramp.

steps.title: The other direction: "In front of the altar" alone might mean south
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now looks at it from the other side. If we only had "אֶל פְּנֵי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ", we might say south. "לִפְנֵי ה׳" pulls it back toward the west.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the verse only said "in front of the altar," I might think the south side. So the verse also says "before ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: In step 6 the ברייתא used "in front of the altar" to stop us from going only west. Now it does the reverse and uses "before ה׳" to stop us from going only south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase in the פסוק checks the other. "לִפְנֵי ה׳" alone points west, and "אֶל פְּנֵי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ" alone points south. Since neither phrase can win outright, the ברייתא needs a spot that satisfies both, and that answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: "In front of the altar", which this ברייתא reads as the south side
"Before ה׳", which this ברייתא reads as the west side, toward the היכל
"I might have thought", which introduces a wrong idea that the פסוק will correct
"The verse teaches", which brings in the words that correct the wrong idea

phrases.english: If it said only "in front of the altar," I might think at the south?
phrases.notes: Both phrases come from the same פסוק about the מנחה (ויקרא 6:7).

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "Before ה׳."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the mirror image of step 6. Step 6 corrected the west reading, and this step corrects the south reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase "לִפְנֵי ה׳" stops us from reading the פסוק as the south side only.

steps.title: The answer: the point of the southwest corner
steps.stepSummary: To satisfy both phrases, the כהן brings the מנחה to the southwest corner, right at its pointed edge, and that is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? He brings it near at the southwest corner, facing the very edge of the corner, and that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the first view's final answer. The southwest corner is both a little west and a little south, so it fits both phrases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither the west reading nor the south reading wins. The ברייתא picks the one spot where west and south meet, the tip of the southwest corner. "וְדַיּוֹ" tells us that standing exactly there fully satisfies the requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: "How so?", used to bring two sources together into one answer
He brings it near, which is the הַגָּשָׁה of the מנחה to the מזבח
The southwest corner of the מזבח
Its point or sharp edge
"And that is enough"

steps.whatToRemember: According to the first view in the ברייתא, the מנחה is brought to the tip of the southwest corner. This is the same spot that steps 3–4 linked to the bird חטאת.

phrases.english: How so?
He brings it near at the southwest corner
facing the edge of the corner, and that is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step brings together the two corrections from steps 6 and 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מנחה is brought near at the tip of the southwest corner, and that is enough.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: west of the corner or south of it? A rule for two verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks whether the כהן may bring it to the west side of the corner or to the south side. He then states a rule: follow the reading that fulfills both phrases, not the one that cancels the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: I might think he can bring it to the west of the corner or to the south of the corner. You must say a rule: whenever there are two verses, and one fulfills itself and the other too, while the other fulfills itself but cancels the first, we drop the one that cancels and hold onto the one that fulfills both.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר opens a second view and sets up a general rule for choosing between two readings. The next step will apply this rule to our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view stood exactly at the corner's tip. רבי אליעזר asks which side of the corner is right. He does not split the difference. Instead he uses a tool: one reading may satisfy both phrases while the other leaves one phrase unfulfilled, and then we go with the reading that satisfies both.

keyTerms.meaning: Two verses, or here two phrases of the פסוק
Fulfills itself and fulfills the other one too
Cancels the other one, meaning the other phrase is left with no meaning
We set aside or drop
We take hold of and follow

steps.confusionAlert: Here "two verses" really means the two phrases of one פסוק: "לִפְנֵי ה׳" and "אֶל פְּנֵי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ".
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule for reading פסוקים: when you must choose between readings, the one that gives meaning to every phrase is preferred.

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says:
I might think he may bring it near to the west of the corner
or to the south of the corner?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַרְתָּ: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא שְׁנֵי מִקְרָאוֹת,
phrases.english: You must say: anywhere you find two verses,
one fulfills itself and fulfills the other,
and one fulfills itself and cancels the other,

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחִין זֶה שֶׁמְּקַיֵּים עַצְמוֹ וּמְבַטֵּל חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: we leave the one that fulfills itself and cancels the other,

phrases.aramaic: וְתוֹפְשִׂין אֶת שֶׁמְּקַיֵּים עַצְמוֹ וּמְקַיֵּים חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: and take hold of the one that fulfills itself and fulfills the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל יַגִּישֶׁנָּה לְמַעֲרָבָהּ שֶׁל קֶרֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second תנא's approach to the same פסוק, and it differs from the first view in step 8. Instead of the tip of the corner, it asks whether the west side or the south side of the corner is meant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one reading fulfills both phrases and the other cancels one of them, follow the reading that fulfills both.

steps.title: Applying the rule: the south fulfills both phrases
steps.stepSummary: Going west leaves "in front of the altar" unfulfilled. Going south also fulfills "before ה׳". So the south is chosen.
steps.simpleTranslation: When you say "before ה׳" means the west, where have you fulfilled "in front of the altar"? But when you say "in front of the altar" means the south, you have also fulfilled "before ה׳".
steps.whatsHappening: The rule from step 9 is now applied to our case. It answers רבי אליעזר's question in favor of the south side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The west reading cancels the phrase "in front of the altar". The south reading keeps both phrases alive. By the rule, we follow the south.

keyTerms.meaning: You have fulfilled, meaning you gave this phrase its meaning
Where, in the sense of "how is it accounted for?"
At the west

phrases.english: When you say "before ה׳" means at the west,
where have you fulfilled "in front of the altar"?
But when you say "in front of the altar" means at the south,
you have fulfilled "before ה׳" too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This applies step 9's general rule to the two phrases about the מנחה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The south side of the corner is correct, because only the south fulfills both phrases.

steps.title: How does the south count as "before ה׳"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim from step 10. How can the south side be called "before ה׳"?
steps.simpleTranslation: At the south, where have you fulfilled "before ה׳"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the claim that the south fulfills both phrases. It sets up רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 simply said that the south also fulfills "before ה׳". Yet "before ה׳" seemed to mean the west, toward the היכל. The גמרא wants to know what makes the south count as "before ה׳".

keyTerms.meaning: At the south

phrases.english: At the south, where have you fulfilled "before ה׳"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges the last line of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that bringing the מנחה at the south also fulfills "לִפְנֵי ה׳".
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "לִפְנֵי ה׳" was understood as the west side, so it is unclear how the south fits it.

steps.title: רב אשי: this תנא holds the whole מזבח stood in the north
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that this תנא holds the entire מזבח stood in the northern half of the עזרה. So its south side still faces the היכל and counts as "before ה׳".
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This תנא holds that the whole altar stood in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge from step 11 by explaining how this תנא pictures the מזבח's location.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מזבח sat entirely in the northern half of the עזרה, its southern side lines up with the middle, right opposite the היכל's entrance. Being opposite the היכל is what "before ה׳" means. So the south side counts as "before ה׳" too.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, meaning his view is
This תנא, here meaning רבי אליעזר
The entire מזבח stood in the north

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר the מנחה is brought at the south side of the southwest corner. That works because he holds the whole מזבח was in the north, so its south side faces the היכל and is "before ה׳".

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
This תנא holds
that the entire altar stood in the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: קָסָבַר הַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the תנא's underlying view of the מזבח's location
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Before ה׳" can only mean the west side, so the south cannot fulfill it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the whole מזבח stood in the north, its south side is opposite the היכל and counts as "before ה׳".

steps.title: What does the משנה mean by 'valid in any place'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that a חטאת העוף is valid anywhere on the מזבח and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'In any place it was valid,' and so on. What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה about the חטאת העוף and asks what that line means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה first says the bird sin offering is done at the southwest corner. Then it says it is valid anywhere, 'but this was its place.' That sounds like it is saying two opposite things, so the גמרא asks what the משנה really means.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird sin offering
Valid; the offering works
What is it saying? The גמרא is asking for the real meaning of a confusing line

phrases.english: In any place it was valid, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the line: 'but this was its place,' meaning the southwest corner.

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the משנה, moving from the מנחה to the חטאת העוף.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can the משנה say the offering is valid anywhere and also name one specific place as its place?

steps.title: רב אשי: pinching anywhere, sprinkling at the corner
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that 'anywhere' refers to the מליקה, while the southwest corner is the place for the הזאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: this is what the משנה means. Any place on the מזבח was valid for pinching the bird. But the southwest corner was the place for sprinkling its blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question by splitting the משנה's two phrases between two different steps of the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two phrases are not about the same action. 'Valid anywhere' is about the מליקה, the pinching of the bird's neck. 'This was its place' is about the הזאה, the sprinkling of the blood. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Pinching the back of a bird's neck with the כהן's fingernail; the way a bird offering is killed
Sprinkling of the blood on the מזבח
This is what it means; introduces a rereading of a text

steps.whatToRemember: In the משנה, 'valid anywhere' refers to the מליקה. The southwest corner is the place for the הזאה.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: This is what it is saying:
In any place it was valid for its pinching,
but this was its place for its sprinkling.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the southwest corner of the מזבח that the משנה named.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Valid anywhere' applies to the מליקה. The southwest corner is the required place for the הזאה.

steps.title: The משנה matches a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה, read this way, teaches the same thing as a ברייתא about the חטאת העוף, and quotes that ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned in our משנה what the רבנן taught in a ברייתא: If the כהן pinched the bird anywhere on the מזבח, it is valid. If he sprinkled its blood anywhere, it is valid. If he sprinkled but did not squeeze out the blood, it is valid. The condition is that he puts some of the blood that comes out at death below the red line.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב אשי's reading of the משנה fits a ברייתא, then quotes the ברייתא. This also sets up the next question about the ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's first line, 'pinching anywhere is valid,' is the same as רב אשי's reading of the משנה. The ברייתא also adds rules about the blood: sprinkling anywhere, a case with no squeezing out, and a requirement to put blood below the חוט הסיקרא.

keyTerms.meaning: The red line painted around the middle of the מזבח's height
The 'blood of the soul,' the blood that comes out as the animal dies

phrases.english: We learned that which the Rabbis taught:
If he pinched it in any place on the altar, it is valid.
If he sprinkled its blood in any place, it is valid,
if he sprinkled but did not squeeze out, it is valid,
phrases.notes: For this offering, after sprinkling, the rest of the blood is normally squeezed out onto the wall of the מזבח (ויקרא 5:9).

phrases.english: provided that he puts, from the red line
and below, from the blood of the soul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב אשי's reading of the משנה matches what a ברייתא teaches outright.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's reading that the מליקה is valid anywhere on the מזבח
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: 'מלקה בכל מקום במזבח כשירה'

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means, since it allows sprinkling anywhere but then requires blood below the red line.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the ברייתא it just quoted and asks what it means, because two of its lines seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says sprinkling the blood 'in any place' is valid. Then it requires that blood be put specifically below the חוט הסיקרא. Both cannot be true about the same blood, so the גמרא asks for the real meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: In any place
Provided that; a condition that limits what was just said
Below

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can the ברייתא allow sprinkling anywhere and also require blood below the red line?

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא: squeezing out may be anywhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to reread the ברייתא so that 'anywhere' refers to the מיצוי, the squeezing out of the blood, and not to the sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: If he pinched the bird anywhere on the מזבח, it is valid. If he squeezed out its blood anywhere on the מזבח, it is valid,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by restating the ברייתא with corrected wording. The answer continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pinching line stays the same. The second line is now read as 'squeezed out its blood anywhere,' not 'sprinkled its blood anywhere.' So the freedom to use any place belongs to the מיצוי, which removes the clash with the sprinkling rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Squeezing out the rest of the bird's blood onto the wall of the מזבח
He squeezed out its blood
The altar

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up הזאה (sprinkling) with מיצוי (squeezing out). In this rereading, only the מיצוי is said to be valid 'anywhere'.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
If he pinched it in any place on the altar, it is valid.

phrases.aramaic: מִיצָּה דָּמָהּ בְּכׇל מָקוֹם בַּמִּזְבֵּחַ – כְּשֵׁירָה,
phrases.english: If he squeezed out its blood in any place on the altar, it is valid,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question from step 16 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows sprinkling the blood anywhere, which clashes with the rule requiring blood below the red line.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'anywhere' line is about squeezing out the blood (מיצוי), not sprinkling it. The full answer continues after this point.
